question.prompt:
Let \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(a_{2018}\) be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers such that

\[a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{2018} = 2018^{2018}.\]

What is the remainder when \(a_1^3 + a_2^3 + \cdots + a_{2018}^3\) is divided by \(6?\)

solutions.title: Reduce cubes and use a power cycle
solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that an integer and its cube always have the same remainder upon division by 6. Indeed,
\[
n^3-n=(n-1)n(n+1).
\]
Among three consecutive integers, at least one is even and at least one is divisible by 3. Their product is therefore divisible by 6, so \(n^3\equiv n\pmod6\).

Applying this to every term gives
\[
a_1^3+\cdots+a_{2018}^3
\equiv a_1+\cdots+a_{2018}
=2018^{2018}\pmod6.
\]
Since \(2018\equiv2\pmod6\), we need the remainder of \(2^{2018}\). The powers of 2 have remainders \(2,4,2,4,\ldots\): multiplying by 2 sends remainder 2 to 4 and remainder 4 back to 2. The exponent 2018 is even, so the requested remainder is \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
